dataset_metadata.disclaimer: New AI-generated English drafts of the recorded Classical Chinese; not scholarly reviewed. Original source interpretations are not verified geometry or modern etymology.

shuowen:9401.text: 鎕銻 is the substance called 火齊. Formed from 金, with 唐 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9402.text: The substance called 鎕銻. Formed from 金, with 弟 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9403.text: Rounded or transformed into a circle, apparently. Formed from 金, with 化 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9404.text: To hang downward. Alternatively, a thousand-jin hammer. Formed from 金, with 敦 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9405.text: Soft 𨮯 metal. Formed from 金 and 柔; 柔 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:9406.text: Blunt. Formed from 金, with 周 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9407.text: Blunt. Formed from 金, with 屯 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9408.text: Sharp. Formed from 金, with 𠂔 indicating the sound. Read like 齊.

shuowen:9409.text: The sense of being at the side. Formed from 金, with 委 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9410.text: A weapon. Formed from 金, with 瞿 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9411.text: To record. Formed from 金, with 名 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9412.text: A metal lock, a door fastening. Formed from 金, with 𧴪 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9413.text: A metal floral ornament. Formed from 金, with 田 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9414.text: An arm ring. Formed from 金, with 川 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9415.text: A kind of hairpin. Formed from 金, with 叉 indicating the sound. Originally written only 叉; this character was added by later people.

shuowen:9416.text: To split. Formed from 金 and 爪.

shuowen:9417.text: Level. It depicts two 干 set opposite, level at the top. All characters in this group are formed from 幵. Xu Xuan says: '幵 only depicts objects being level; it has no sound or meaning of its own.'

shuowen:9418.text: To scoop and take. A pictograph, with contents inside, sharing the conception of 包. All characters in this group are formed from 勺.

shuowen:9419.text: To bestow or give. One 勺 makes 与. This 与 is the same as 與.

shuowen:9420.text: A support on which to lean. A pictograph. The Rites of Zhou lists five supports: jade, carved, red, lacquered, and plain. All characters in this group are formed from 几.

shuowen:9421.text: To lean on a support. Formed from 几 and 任. The Book of Zhou says: 'Leaning on the jade support.' Read like 馮.

shuowen:9422.text: To dwell or stay. Formed from 尸 obtaining 几 and stopping. The Classic of Filial Piety says: 'Zhongni was dwelling.' 凥 here means being at leisure.

shuowen:9423.text: To stop. Obtaining a support, one stops. Formed from 几 and 夂.

shuowen:9424.text: An offering stand. Formed from 几, with two cross-strokes at its feet and 一 as the ground below. All characters in this group are formed from 且.

shuowen:9425.text: A ritual offering stand. Formed from half of 肉 upon 且.

shuowen:9426.text: To go for the time being. Formed from 且, with 豦 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9427.text: To cut wood. A pictograph. All characters in this group are formed from 斤.

shuowen:9428.text: To chop. Formed from 斤, with 父 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9429.text: An axe with a square socket. Formed from 斤, with 爿 indicating the sound. The Odes says: 'And chipped my axe.'

shuowen:9430.text: To strike. Formed from 斤, with 石 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9431.text: To chop. Formed from 斤, with 句 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9432.text: To chop. Formed from 斤, with 屬 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9433.text: To chop. Formed from 斤 and 𠁁.

shuowen:9434.text: To cut evenly or sever. Formed from 斤 and 金.

shuowen:9435.text: The sound of chopping wood. Formed from 斤, with 戶 indicating the sound. The Odes says: 'Chopping wood, suo suo.'

shuowen:9436.text: To split. Formed from 斤, with 其 indicating the sound. The Odes says: 'Split it with an axe.'

shuowen:9437.text: To cut off. Formed from 斤, with 昔 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9438.text: To cut off. Formed from 斤 and 𢇍. 𢇍 is ancient-script 絕.

shuowen:9439.text: To strike with an axe handle. Formed from 斤, with 良 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9440.text: To take wood. Formed from 斤, with 新 indicating the sound, as recorded in the source.

shuowen:9441.text: Two axes. Formed from two 斤.

shuowen:9442.text: Ten sheng. A pictograph, with a handle. All characters in this group are formed from 斗.

shuowen:9443.text: Ten dou. Formed from 斗, with 角 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9444.text: A jade 爵 vessel. Xia called it 琖, Yin 斝, and Zhou 爵. Formed from 吅 and 斗, with 冂 depicting its shape; the same conception as 爵. Some say a 斝 holds six dou.

shuowen:9445.text: To measure. Formed from 斗, with 米 inside. Read like 遼.

shuowen:9446.text: A measure. Formed from 斗, with 臾 indicating the sound. The Rites of Zhou says: 'Three 斞 of lacquer.'

shuowen:9447.text: The handle of a gourd ladle. Formed from 斗, with 倝 indicating the sound. Yang Xiong and Du Lin both explain it as the 斡 of a light carriage's wheel.

shuowen:9448.text: A soup ladle. Formed from 斗, with 鬼 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9449.text: To level a dou or hu measure. Formed from 斗, with 冓 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9450.text: To ladle. Formed from 斗, with 甚 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9451.text: To draw or pour out. Formed from 斗, with 余 indicating the sound. Read like 荼.

shuowen:9452.text: To scoop out. Formed from 斗, with 𥇛 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9453.text: To measure a thing and divide it in half. Formed from 斗 and 半; 半 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:9454.text: A measure overflowing. Formed from 斗, with 㫄 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9455.text: To ladle full. Formed from 斗, with 䜌 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9456.text: Exchanging things of equal amount is called 斣. Formed from 斗, with 蜀 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9457.text: A hu measure has a 𣂀 at its side. Formed from 斗, with 𠩓 indicating the sound. Alternatively, projecting; alternatively, sharp. The Erya says: '𣂀 is called 疀,' an ancient agricultural implement.

shuowen:9458.text: Ten yue. Formed from 斗, also a pictograph.

shuowen:9459.text: The 酋 spear, erected on a war carriage, two zhang long. A pictograph. All characters in this group are formed from 矛.

shuowen:9460.text: A kind of spear. Formed from 矛, with 良 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9461.text: A kind of spear. Formed from 矛, with 害 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9462.text: A kind of spear. Formed from 矛, with 昔 indicating the sound. Read like 笮.

shuowen:9463.text: A spear shaft. Formed from 矛, with 今 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9464.text: To stab. Formed from 矛, with 丑 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9465.text: The general name for the carriage body and wheels. Made by Xi Zhong in the Xia rulers' time. A pictograph. All characters in this group are formed from 車.

shuowen:9466.text: A carriage with a curved shaft and enclosing sides. Formed from 車, with 干 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9467.text: A screened carriage at the front, a covered carriage at the rear, according to the source's compressed description. Formed from 車, with 甾 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9468.text: A screened carriage, 輜車. Formed from 車, with 并 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9469.text: A sleeping carriage. Formed from 車, with 𥁕 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9470.text: A sleeping carriage. Formed from 車, with 京 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9471.text: A small carriage. Formed from 車, with 召 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9472.text: A light carriage. Formed from 車, with 坙 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9473.text: A light carriage. Formed from 車, with 酋 indicating the sound. The Odes says: 'A light carriage with bells on the bits.'

shuowen:9474.text: A war carriage. Formed from 車, with 朋 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9475.text: A war carriage. Formed from 車, with 屯 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9476.text: A carriage for breaking battle formations. Formed from 車, with 童 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9477.text: A tall military carriage with a raised nest-like platform for observing the enemy. Formed from 車, with 巢 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: 'The ruler of Chu mounted the observation carriage.'

shuowen:9478.text: A carriage body. Formed from 車, with 舁 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9479.text: A carriage being harmoniously assembled. Formed from 車, with 咠 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9480.text: The cover of a covered carriage. Formed from 車, with 曼 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9481.text: The part before a carriage's crossbar. Formed from 車, with 凡 indicating the sound. The Rites of Zhou says: 'Stand facing the front 軓.'

shuowen:9482.text: The front of a carriage. Formed from 車, with 式 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9483.text: A crosspiece before the carriage railing. Formed from 車, with 各 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9484.text: A curved bronze fitting above the carriage's 騎 component; its precise position is unclear. Formed from 車, with 爻 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9485.text: A carriage's side projections turned outward. Formed from 車 and 反; 反 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:9486.text: A carriage's crosswise railing. Formed from 車, with 對 indicating the sound. The Rites of Zhou says: 'Divide the 軹 circumference into three; remove one to obtain the 轛 circumference.'

shuowen:9487.text: The side of a carriage. Formed from 車, with 奇 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9488.text: The two side panels of a carriage. Formed from 車, with 𦔮 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9489.text: A carriage's binding or ornament, apparently. Formed from 車, with 川 indicating the sound. The Rites of Zhou says: 'An isolated minister rides a 夏䡅 carriage.' Alternatively, a carriage for lowering a coffin is called 䡅.

shuowen:9490.text: A carriage's interlaced framework. Formed from 車, with 嗇 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9491.text: A crosspiece within a carriage's framework. Formed from 車, with 令 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9492.text: The front crosspiece of a light carriage. Formed from 車, with 君 indicating the sound. Read like 帬; also like 褌.

shuowen:9493.text: The rear crosspiece of a carriage. Formed from 車, with 㐱 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9494.text: A carriage's 'crouching rabbit' axle support. Formed from 車, with 菐 indicating the sound. The Rites of Zhou says: 'Add the rear crosspiece and axle support.'

shuowen:9495.text: Leather beneath a carriage's axle support. Formed from 車, with 𡖀 indicating the sound. 𡖀 is ancient 昏. Read like 閔.

shuowen:9496.text: That which supports the wheels. Formed from 車, with 由 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9497.text: A binding for the carriage axle. Formed from 車, with 复 indicating the sound. The Changes says: 'The carriage loses its axle binding.'

shuowen:9498.text: Something that stops a carriage. Formed from 車, with 刃 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9499.text: A carriage's stopping block, according to the recorded 車軔 gloss. Formed from 車, with 柔 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9500.text: A carriage-wheel shaping circle or frame, apparently. Alternatively, a one-wheeled carriage. Formed from 車, with abbreviated 熒 indicating the sound. Read like 煢.
